ledger.note: 1805: Cliopatria's row for the colonial empire begins. The page dates the empire's start to 27 July 1605 ('The story of France's colonial empire truly began on 27 July 1605', Port Royal in Acadia) and calls the 'first French colonial empire' the one that 'existed until 1814'. Earlier centuries are Cliopatria's New France (1609-1791), French India (1673-1847) and French Guiana rows; this dossier maps the remnant from 1805.

notes: IS IT THE FIRST FRENCH EMPIRE? No. 'First French colonial empire' shares Wikidata Q71084 with 'First French Empire' in Cliopatria, but the Wikipedia article is 'French colonial empire' and describes an overseas empire that began on 27 July 1605 and 'existed until 1814' under successive regimes; the Napoleonic state is its own dossier (first-french-empire), which excludes the overseas cells. Cliopatria's row is a 438.6 km2 sliver of 16 polygons (Saint-Pierre and Miquelon to a point in Wisconsin) that rasterises to no land cell; both shapes are verdict wrong. START: the page dates the empire to 1605, but Cliopatria draws New France (1609-1791), French India (1673-1847) and French Guiana (the 1791 row) separately, so this dossier starts at Cliopatria's 1805 and the 1805 found event is confidence 1; extending the start to 1605 would double-draw those rows. NOT ON THE PAGES: the year each colony fell to Britain (the page says only 'when war resumed in 1803, the British soon recaptured them'); the Mascarenes' 1810 capture (the 1811 event rests on Cliopatria's shapes); whether Saint-Pierre and Miquelon were British-held; Santo Domingo, which the Treaty page 'returned to Spain' in 1814 (Art. VIII), is not in Cliopatria's shape and is not drawn; Chandernagore and Pondicherry are not itemised by the colonial page (the Treaty page does not mention them). The treaty page lists Martinique, Guiana, Réunion, Senegal and the Indian posts as 'not on page'; the colonial page supplies them. Haiti's independence in 1804 and the sale of Louisiana in 1803 precede the 1805 start and are in other dossiers (haiti, french-louisiana). CLIOPATRIA NEIGHBOURS: british-colonial-empire 1805-1814 and united-states-of-america, as counterpart only. NOT COVERED (page budget, two pages): the 1605-1804 history. GAZETTEER NAMES NEEDED: none.
